document_check.note: Lu H, Liu J, Gu G, Li X, Yin S, Cui D. Nonlinear Phase Synchronization Analysis of EEG Signals in Amnesic Mild Cognitive Impairment with Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus. Neuroscience 472 (2021) 25-34. 27 T2DM participants (17 aMCI, 10 cognitively normal controls), resting EEG compared between groups; no predictive model. Matches the cited study (Lu et al. 2021).

cited_result: Lower resting-state EEG nonlinear phase synchronisation (CPR) in 17 aMCI patients than in 10 cognitively normal controls, all with type 2 diabetes (Mann-Whitney U with FDR correction): significant for several intrahemispheric frontal, parietal and temporal electrode pairs, not significant for interhemispheric pairs.
tool_reason: The cited result compares an EEG measure between aMCI and control groups at one time point within a single recruited T2DM sample, which is a cross-sectional group comparison and not a model or accuracy study. Item mapping used: exposure = cognitive group assignment, condition = diagnostic criteria (T2DM, aMCI), outcome = the CPR synchronisation value.

domains.domain: Item 1: Criteria for inclusion in the sample clearly defined
domains.rationale: Explicit inclusion criteria for both groups and a list of exclusions (neurological disease, macrovascular complications, CNS drugs, alcohol, depression) are given.

signalling.question: Were the criteria for inclusion in the sample clearly defined?
signalling.quote: Inclusion criteria of the aMCI group were (1) with the hypomnesia of chief complaint, (2) absence of repercussions on daily life, (3) Clinical evaluation conﬁrmed cognitive impairment, in this paper the MMSE and MoCA tests were used to evaluate cognitive function and the MoCA score < 26.

domains.domain: Item 2: Study subjects and setting described in detail
domains.rationale: Setting and age, education and sex are reported, but for a T2DM sample the diabetes characteristics (duration, glycaemic control, treatment) are not reported, and recruitment period and method (consecutive or convenience) are not stated.

signalling.question: Were the study subjects and the setting described in detail?
signalling.quote: The patients were from the Neurology Department of the Rocket Force Special Medical Center of Chinese People’s Liberation Army in China. [Searched for: recruitment dates, recruitment method, diabetes duration, HbA1c, glucose-lowering treatment; none reported. Table 2 reports only age, education and neuropsychological scores.]

domains.domain: Item 3: Exposure (cognitive group assignment) measured validly and reliably
domains.rationale: All participants received the same standardised neuropsychological battery (MMSE, MoCA, AVLT, BNT, fluency, digit span, TMT, ADL) used for group assignment; assessor details are not given.

signalling.question: Was the exposure measured in a valid and reliable way?
signalling.quote: All participants underwent general demographic and a series of standardized neuropsychological assessments.

domains.domain: Item 4: Objective, standard criteria used for measurement of the condition
domains.rationale: T2DM was defined by WHO criteria and aMCI by referenced criteria with a MoCA cut-off, but the amnesic label rests on a subjective memory complaint plus a global MoCA score; no objective memory-impairment criterion is stated, and MMSE did not differ between groups.

signalling.question: Were objective, standard criteria used for measurement of the condition?
signalling.quote: According to the inclusion and exclusion criteria for aMCI group (Cui et al., 2015), the T2DM subjects were divided into two groups.

domains.rationale: Age and education were identified as factors to be controlled by matching, and CNS-active drugs, alcoholism and depression were identified as exclusions. Sex and diabetes-specific factors were not considered.

signalling.question: Were confounding factors identified?
signalling.quote: The other group included 10 age and educational level matched subjects (6 males, 4 females) with normal cognitive function as the control group.

domains.domain: Item 6: Strategies to deal with confounding stated
domains.rationale: Group matching on age and education (checked by non-significant tests) and restriction by exclusion criteria are stated; the CPR comparison itself is unadjusted, and sex (7/10 versus 6/4) is not matched.

signalling.question: Were strategies to deal with confounding factors stated?
signalling.quote: In terms of demographic characteristics, there was no signiﬁcant diﬀerence between the two groups, i.e., they were matched in age and education level.

domains.domain: Item 7: Outcome (EEG synchronisation) measured validly and reliably
domains.rationale: Standard EEG acquisition, but artefacts were removed by visual inspection with no statement that the specialists were blind to group, CPR parameters were set empirically, and no reliability data exist for CPR in cognitive impairment (the authors describe it as applied for the first time).

signalling.question: Were the outcomes measured in a valid and reliable way?
signalling.quote: The ocular, muscular and other types of artifacts in the raw EEG data were removed visually by EEG specialists, then the data was re-sampled to 500 Hz. ... According to the previous experience, we choose the empirical value m = 3

domains.rationale: Non-parametric tests were chosen after normality and variance checks, with FDR correction across the many electrode pairs; suitable for a small unadjusted two-group comparison.

signalling.question: Was appropriate statistical analysis used?
signalling.quote: There were multiple comparison problems in the statistical analysis on the CPR values of many diﬀerent electrodes, so the False Discovery Rate (FDR) correction was used for multiple comparison correction

applicability.rationale: Every participant has T2DM and the controls are cognitively normal diabetic patients; the authors note there is no comparison with a non-diabetic population. The result applies to aMCI within T2DM only.

overall: Some concerns (JBI analytical cross-sectional: items 1, 3, 5, 6 and 8 Yes; items 2, 4 and 7 Unclear; none of the four critical items No)
overall_rationale: No critical item is No, so under the review's rule the result is not high risk. Concerns remain: an unblinded visual artefact-rejection step and an EEG index with no reliability data (item 7), an aMCI definition without an objective memory criterion (item 4), an unadjusted analysis with only group-level matching on age and education, and a very small sample (17 versus 10), which the authors acknowledge.
